name: Config / Hardcode / Secret Placement

checks.check: No secrets committed to Git (including Git history)
No secrets in logs or debug output
No server secrets exposed to client bundle / frontend
Critical env vars have typed validation before the feature uses them; required startup dependencies fail fast when missing.
Env access and validation have clear owners; avoid scattered reads that give the same setting inconsistent meaning.
Business invariants live in code; configurable business policy has an explicit owner, validation and precedence rather than hidden environment-driven behavior.
Operational switches that must change at runtime come from an appropriate reloadable configuration source, with explicit freshness and ownership.
Infrastructure defaults must be explicit and safe for the selected environment; missing required deployment values must not silently select another authority or destination.
Each resolved config value has one owner and explicit precedence; multiple input sources must not produce conflicting effective truth.
Client-visible config is explicitly classified as public; server-only config is not pushed to client by convenience
Each supported environment has explicit required values or documented defaults/inheritance; intentional differences are accounted for.
Infrastructure config is separated from business truth — DB URLs, bucket names, etc. are not mixed with business rules or domain constants
.gitignore alone is not secret management: secrets need access-controlled storage and protection from builds/logs/backups, using a vault or an appropriate host facility.
Runtime dynamic config has an explicit freshness strategy (for example bounded TTL or validated invalidation) so cached data cannot silently become stale authority.
A newly required setting must reach the deployment command or manifest.
Where a fallback is provided for an unavailable config service, is the fallback value itself safe — does losing the value open or close?
Can you say, from the diff, which entry a secret arrived through?
Assess secret retrieval against the host’s actual facilities and threat model; use supported protected retrieval or required environment injection without assuming a vault is always available.

anti_patterns: Secrets stored in repo constants or committed `.env` files
Fixed business invariants hidden in environment switches instead of their declared owner
Runtime mutable config treated as code constants
Skipping typed validation of loaded configuration
Same config duplicated across env, code constants, and DB without authority rule
Scattered reads give the same environment setting inconsistent meaning
